name: Scan Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever job boards daily and send new matches to Slack

parameters.content:
## Scan Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever job boards daily and send new matches to Slack

### Who's it for

Anyone who watches a fixed list of companies rather than a job aggregator: recruiters tracking competitors, founders watching who is hiring, and job hunters who would rather read four boards themselves than trust a feed. Aggregators keep copies of dead postings; these endpoints are the employer's own board, so what you see is what is actually open.

### How it works

One Set node holds the whole configuration: the boards to watch and the words that decide what counts as a match. The workflow builds one request per board, fetches each public posting API, normalises four different response shapes into the same row, and filters by title and location. Anything it has already sent you is dropped by the Remove Duplicates node, which remembers keys across executions, so you only ever see what is new. What survives is posted to Slack as a single message.

### How to set up

1. Open **Boards and filters** and put your own boards in. The slug is the company's board name in the URL: jobs.ashbyhq.com/COMPANY, boards.greenhouse.io/COMPANY, jobs.lever.co/COMPANY.
2. Edit the keyword lists in the same node. title_any is an OR list and title_none excludes. Words of up to three letters (ai, eu) match whole words only; longer words and phrases match anywhere. List the countries and regions you can work from in location_any, not just "remote". The remote flag alone is not trusted, because some boards set it on office roles: location_any is checked against the location text, and only a remote posting with no location text passes on the flag alone. location_none always applies.
3. Add a Slack credential and set your channel, or replace that node with Gmail, Telegram or a Google Sheet.
4. Run it once manually. The first run will match a lot, because nothing has been seen yet.

### Requirements

Self-hosted or cloud n8n, and a Slack credential if you keep the Slack step. The job boards need no key: these are the same public endpoints the companies' own career pages call.

### How to customize

Recruitee is already supported in the code — add `{ "ats": "recruitee", "slug": "yourcompany" }` to the board list. To add another ATS, put its URL in **Build board requests** and its response shape in **Normalise and match**; both are small, commented functions. To keep a history instead of a notification, drop a Google Sheets or Postgres node after Remove Duplicates.

## 1 · The only node you edit
Boards to watch and the words that decide a match. Everything downstream reads from here.

## 2 · One request per board
Public posting APIs, no keys. The HTTP node is set to return text so that a board answering with a bare array does not get split into separate items — that keeps each response paired with the board that produced it. A board that fails is logged and skipped.

## 3 · Match, then forget what you have seen
Four response shapes become one row, then title and location filters run. Remove Duplicates remembers the keys it has already let through, across executions, so a posting is announced once.

## 4 · One message, not twenty
The roles are folded into a single Slack message. Swap Slack for Gmail, Telegram or a spreadsheet — the rows are plain JSON.
